SEND Provision
At Seven Mills, we are committed to providing a high quality education for all our children. We are an inclusive school and as a staff, we work hard to provide the help required to ensure that all children make progress in all that they do. We believe there are times when some children need additional support to fully access all aspects of school life. Through our special needs provision, and working collaboratively with parents/carers, outside agencies and local special schools, we endeavour to identify promptly a child’s particular needs so that individualised programmes and support can be provided when appropriate.
This year, our 3 targets to improve our Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) provision are to:
Our SEN information report and ‘Inclusion at Seven Mills’ documents below provide information about the kinds of support your child may receive while they are at Seven Mills.
London Borough of Tower Hamlets has a wide range of services to support your child with SEN. Find out more by clicking on the link below:

Before and After School Clubs
At Seven Mills, we offer a range of clubs to help children discover and develop their talents. Breakfast Club runs from 7:30 until school starts and costs 50p per day to attend. A range of activities are offered each day. See below for an example of the timetable.
Our after school clubs also aim to help children develop resilience and confidence, as they learn to be ready, respectful and responsible. At the beginning of each term, a letter is sent out detailing what clubs are available and children sign up on a first come first served basis. We aim for every child to be able to take part in at least one club. Clubs run from 15:30 – 16:30.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery and Reception September 2025 : Information for Parents – Seven Mills Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to our Seven Mills Early Years! You can find information about your child starting Nursery on this page.
From September 2025, our sessions will run as follows:
9:00 – 15:25 Tuesday
9:00 – 11:15 Wednesday
13:15 – 15:25 Wednesday
9:00 – 15:25 Thursday
FULL TIME: 9:00 – 3.25 (30 hours)
30-Hour Funding for Working Parents
Some children may qualify for 30 hours of free childcare instead of 15, subject to meeting eligibility criteria. More information is available here:
If you are eligible, you will be issued with an 11-digit code via email. Please send this code, along with your National Insurance number, to the school office. We will also ask you to complete a Parental Declaration form to claim the correct number of hours from Tower Hamlets.
If you are not eligible, but wish to pay for a full-time place for your child, this will cost £100 per week and must be paid in advance to the school office. Please speak to the office team if you would like any further information.
Arrival and Morning Routine
At the start of each day, you can drop your child off directly at the Nursery door. You are welcome to come in and help your child settle by hanging up their coat and belongings. Our friendly staff are always available to support children in finding their coat peg, removing their coat and putting away their things.
As part of the morning routine, each child will find their own name and self register, helping them feel part of the group. A member of staff will be at the door to greet families, ensure a safe start to the day and receive any urgent messages. If you’d like a longer conversation about your child, we’ll be happy to arrange a meeting at a mutually convenient time.
Daily Activities and Learning
Children in Nursery enjoy a balanced mix of:
Short carpet sessions take place daily, where children come together to enjoy stories, songs, number games and more. We also offer free-flow access between our indoor and outdoor areas, allowing children to learn in the space that suits them best.
Adult-led activities, carefully planned to support learning
Small group sessions to develop specific skills
End of the Day
At home time, a staff member will open the Early Years gate for you to access the Nursery unit. Children will be waiting on the carpet inside. Staff will call each child’s name before they are safely handed over to you.
If you’d like to speak with a staff member, please wait until most children have been collected so we can ensure every child leaves with the correct adult. Please always let us know in advance if someone different will be collecting your child. They must be over 18 years of age and known to staff.
Learning in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
At Seven Mills, our Nursery follows the EYFS framework, which is designed to support young children’s development and prepare them for school. It is based on 7 key areas of learning:
Prime Areas (the foundations of learning):
Communication and Language
Physical DevelopmentPersonal, Social and Emotional Development
Specific Areas:
Children learn best through play, exploration, and meaningful interactions with others- both indoors and outdoors.
Literacy
Mathematics
Understanding the World
Expressive Arts and Design
What to Wear to Nursery
Children need to wear our school uniform. We have branded uniform items available from the office if you wish, but this is not essential.
Please remember that Nursery can be messy! We use aprons, but please do not send children into school in their best clothes.
We go outside in any weather, so please send your child to school with appropriate clothing.
Please label all clothing clearly with your child’s name.
Navy jumper or cardigan
Navy or black trousers, skirt or leggings
Velcro black shoes
Navy dress
Navy gingham summer dress
White or navy t-shirt or polo shirt
Cold days: coat, scarf, hat and gloves
Wet days: please bring wellies and raincoats
Snacks, Drinks and Lunchtime
Every child is offered fruit and they have access to milk or water daily. Please send your child with a water bottle every day, clearly labelled with their name.
You can either choose for your child to have a school lunch or bring a healthy nut-free packed lunch.
Lunch for Nursery children costs £3 per day. This needs to be paid in advance to the school office.
School lunch is free for children from Reception – Year 6.
The children all eat in the main school hall with support from our Nursery team.
Visitors and Special Events
To enrich learning, we welcome a range of visitors to Nursery – from emergency services to animals! Throughout the year, children also enjoy special events like:
You’ll always be notified in advance and invited to join in wherever possible.
Christmas performances
Dress-up days
Fundraisers
Parent Partnerships
We value strong communication with families. Here’s how we work with you:
We’re always happy to welcome parent helpers—just wait until after the first half-term to allow children to settle.
Starting Nursery
Stay & Play – July
You and your child will be invited to a Stay & Play before they begin. This allows them to explore the Nursery and meet staff with you by their side. Please see your induction letter for the date of this.
Home Visit – First 2 weeks of September
Before your child starts, two members of the Nursery team will visit you at home. This 20-minute visit helps staff get to know your child in a comfortable setting and gives you a chance to ask questions.
Settling In – From Mid September
Children start Nursery slowly to ensure a smooth and positive transition. They begin with shorter sessions before gradually building to their full sessions. Please see your induction letter for the dates of this. If a longer settling period is needed, we’ll work closely with you to arrange this.
Helping Your Child at Home
Children’s language development is key to their learning and well-being. At age 3, children may be:
Using 500–700 words
Enjoying pretend play
Following 2–3 step instructions
Making grammar mistakes—this is part of learning!
Talking and listening every day
Reading their favourite books repeatedly
Encouraging make-believe play
Helpful Resources:
FAQs
What if my child is late?Please sign in at the office before bringing your child to Nursery.
What if my child is sick?For sickness or diarrhoea, keep your child at home for 24 hours after the last episode. Call the school office to report absence.
What if I’m late collecting my child?Your child will be taken to the office and supervised until you arrive. Call ahead if you’re delayed.
Will my child automatically get a school place?No—Nursery attendance doesn’t guarantee a Reception place. You must apply separately.
Is wraparound care available?Currently, we do not offer any additional provision for Nursery-aged children beyond our normal school opening hours
If you need support with additional childcare before or after-school, please contact:
Family Information Service on 020 7364 6495 or look on the towerhamlets.gov.uk website for a local registered childminder.
If you have any questions or would like more information, please speak to Maddy, Momothaj or a member of the Early Years team. We’re here to support your child – and you – every step of the way!

pageCache.pageTitle: PE and Sport Premium – Seven Mills Primary School
pageCache.text:
PE and Sport Premium
What is the Sports Premium?
The government is providing over £320 million in additional funding to improve provision of physical education and sport in primary schools. Schools receive PE and sport premium funding based on the number of pupils in years 1 to 6; this means we receive a total grant for 2025-2026 of £17,719. This funding – provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport – will be allocated to primary school Headteachers and is ring-fenced and therefore can only be spent on provision of PE and sport in schools.
Purpose of the funding:
All schools have to spend the sport funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but there is freedom to choose how we do it. Our aim is to maintain the quality and quantity of sports and afterschool clubs, inter and intra school competitions, as well as to raise opportunities for pupils to try different activities whilst raising participation numbers. At Seven Mills Primary School we recognise the contribution of PE to the health and wellbeing of the children. We believe that an innovative and varied PE curriculum and extracurricular opportunities have a positive influence on the concentration, attitude and academic achievement of all children. Furthermore through sports and physical activity we aim to develop a greater awareness about dangers such as obesity, smoking and other such activities that can have a detrimental impact upon pupil health and well-being. Additionally we believe that sports and extra-curricular clubs play an important role in social inclusion, and self-confidence. The school has a Gold Award for the School Games kitemark which evidences its commitment to school sports.
You can find out more about the PE and Sport premium on the gov.uk website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher Welcome – Seven Mills Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher Welcome
As the headteacher of Seven Mills Primary School, I’d like to wish you the warmest welcome.We are a school with the community at its heart and the children at the centre of all we do. Here, learning is ambitious, exciting and engaging with a caring outlook. We are preparing young minds for the opportunities and challenges of the future.Our curriculum is thought provoking; it aims to empower all of our children with knowledge, skills and the critical curiosity they need to grow a lasting love of learning. We are fostering our children’s self-belief in belonging and their ability to contribute to their communities as local, national and global citizens.Underpinning our values of being ambitious, compassionate and empowered is a keen focus on inclusivity which is lived through our actions and the decisions we make.We enjoy kind, trusting and respectful partnerships with our Seven Mills families and share with them an unwavering belief that we must always keep the children’s best interests at heart.Please come and visit! We’d love you to experience the welcoming atmosphere of the school, and to meet our friendly, hardworking staff and children in action; please contact us to arrange a visit.

Music
At Seven Mills Primary School our vision is for children to experience music and to make musical progress; to become confident and creative musicians and to leave us having found something in music that they feel is for them. We want our learners to be secure in their musicianship skills and experienced in behaving musically by themselves and in ensemble with others. We want them to develop an open-minded attitude, an appreciation for diversity in Music and a respect for their own and others’ differing and developing musical tastes and preferences. We aim to give our learners an awareness of musical possibilities; music for music’s sake but also music as a career.
The design of our music curriculum is informed by the DFE Model Music Curriculum, guidance published in March 2021 which amplifies the statutory requirements of the National Curriculum for Music. Guided by the Model Music Curriculum, our curriculum is carefully planned in units and sequenced to ensure that skills and techniques are introduced, rehearsed, repeated and revisited in an integrated way throughout the academic year as well as year on year, enabling children to grow their musicianship and develop their musical experience and creativity in engaging and meaningful contexts.
Learning in music comprises the skills of Singing, Listening, Improvising, Composing, Performing and Notation (the symbolic representation of musical sounds and musical time). We recognise that singing is foundational to every area of music learning, enabling as it does the experience and embodiment of the conceptual e.g. pulse, rhythm and pitch and the expressive e.g dynamics, tempo etc. and we fully utilise this as children progress through the school. The skills of Singing, Listening, Improvising, Composing, Performing and Notation are integrated and interlinked throughout our curriculum e.g. children mark the pulse of music as they listen, they derive rhythm notation from the songs they sing, they perform the compositions they have created inspired by music they have listened to. As children progress through the units over the course of their primary school life, we aim to ensure that children are able to draw on and apply previously taught and practised skills and techniques as well as to deepen their experience and understanding of the broad history of music.
Music Development Plan
This document is a summary of how our school delivers music education to all our pupils across three areas – curriculum music, co-curricular provision and musical experiences – and what changes we are planning in future years.
